Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported
at an intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?
A: Yes, I understand.
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather use [claimant name] for this, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving when the collision happened?
A: I was heading through a four-way intersection on a residential street. The light had been green for me, or at least I
thought it had been.
Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle came from my right side and hit the passenger door. I felt the impact right away, and my car spun
partway around before stopping against the curb.
Q: Were you injured?
A: I hit my head on the window frame. I didn't lose consciousness, but I've had a bad headache since, I get dizzy
when I stand up too fast, and bright lights bother my eyes. My doctor said it's a concussion.
Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the collision?
A: Yes, I was taken to an urgent care clinic that same day, and I've had two follow-up visits since. I'm still taking it
easy and not driving much.
Q: Did you notice anything unusual about the other driver before the collision?
A: Not really. They seemed to be moving at a normal speed. I was focused on the road ahead.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still recovering, and I'd appreciate it if you could keep me updated on the claim.
Q: Thnak you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>

"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
